findings.title: fileSizes() reports five files that do not exist as 'DID NOT ARRIVE', and fetches the whole suite twice to get there
findings.where: scripts/diagnostics.mjs:1095-1135 (loadedFiles' crawl), 1153-1178 (fileSizes); scripts/api.mjs:1285 (the runTests thunk the crawl follows); scripts/tests-tier0.mjs:18412, 25321-25322 and scripts/tests-kit.mjs:1322-1324 (the fixture strings it reads as imports)
findings.what_happens: loadedFiles crawls from module.mjs every `from "./x.mjs"` and `import("./x.mjs")` it finds in a file's text, comments and string literals included. api.mjs's `import("./tests.mjs")` takes it into the suite (13 files, about 17 MB on disk, shipped in module.zip: .gitattributes does not leave them out), and the suite's fixtures and comments name x.mjs, y.mjs, b.mjs, lazy.mjs and missing.mjs. Each is fetched, fails, is kept in the list (`scripts.add(file)` before the `text === null` test), and fileSizes then prints it as `HTTP 404  ← DID NOT ARRIVE`. Every suite file is fetched once by the crawl and again with cache: "reload" by fileSizes. A static run of the same regex from module.mjs over today's tree reaches 276 names for 271 files in scripts/: the five extra are those fixtures.
findings.failure_scenario: A GM on a hosted world told to run `await game.drpg.fileSizes()` after an update pastes a report that says five module files did not arrive, on an install where every file did, after the browser pulled about 34 MB of test scripts past its cache.
findings.expected: The list the tool exists to give: the files a table loads, the suite at most as one line, and no name that is only text inside a test; a file that 404s because it does not exist in the repository is not a file of the module.
findings.refutation_tried: Looked for a filter on the crawl (none: the only test is `scripts.has(file)`), for a reason the suite should be listed (the header 1069-1093 argues for following lazy imports so an edited file is seen, which the suite is not at a table), and for a test pinning the list's shape: R126 (tests-tier0.mjs:5663-5683) checks only that the manifest's stylesheets, languages, module.json and module.mjs are present, not that nothing else is. Ran the same regex over the source in Python from module.mjs: 276 names reached, 271 files exist, the five missing are exactly x, y, b, lazy and missing. The double fetch is read from the two `fetch` calls (1103, 1165); its byte count on a hosted server is not measured.

findings.title: game.drpg.diagnoseDespair() on a player's browser prints the newest roll of the world, a whisper to other users included; diagnose() marks the same part GM-only
findings.where: scripts/diagnostics.mjs:210-220 (the newest roll, no visibility filter), 2228 (the part gmOnly in the one report); scripts/api.mjs:1195 (diagnoseDespair on game.drpg, no gate); compare scripts/diagnostics.mjs:68-70 (the dice part's filter, E52-15)
findings.what_happens: diagnoseDespair picks `[...game.messages].reverse().find(m => rolls)` with no `visible` test, prints its type, `speaker.actor` and the subject rollSubjectNow names, and logs Daggerheart's reading of its duality (readDuality) to the console. On a player's browser that message can be another user's whisper: every browser receives every message (utils.mjs:794-799). The one report runs this part only on a GM (`gmOnly: true`), and its dice part filters to `m.visible !== false` for exactly this reason, but the console command on game.drpg runs it for anyone. A roll the module throws is emptied of its speaker (private-rolls.mjs:18-25, 818-827), so for those the line names nobody; what stays is the rolls the module did not throw - Daggerheart's own item rolls, a Monocub's Meddle, a /r, a sheet statistic thrown with no GM connected - whose speaker the document keeps.
findings.failure_scenario: A player asked by the GM to paste `game.drpg.diagnoseDespair()` because their Despair is not counting posts a card that names the student whose whispered item roll came last, and the console line under it says whether that roll landed with Hope or Fear.
findings.expected: The direct call holds to the rule the one report holds it to: on a player, only rolls that player may see, or the GM-only answer the report gives.
findings.refutation_tried: Checked that the data is already in the player's browser (utils.mjs:794-799: it is, so a console could read it; the finding is that the module paints it, which E52-15 fixed for the dice part only). Checked that module-thrown rolls are neutral (private-rolls.mjs:700-725): they are, which narrows the exposure to the rolls named above. Checked who sees the card: the caller alone (utils.mjs:782-789). Looked for a gate on game.drpg.diagnoseDespair (api.mjs:1195: none) and inside the function (194-200 only add a sentence for a player). Not measured on a real table: what a non-recipient's copy of a whispered Daggerheart item roll holds.

findings.title: The four explainer windows never redraw: their 'right now' lines stay as they were when the window opened
findings.where: scripts/explain.mjs:49-58 (one drpgWindow, nothing kept live), 187-225 (room, Search Tokens left), 279-315 (every pool's count, the Overflow hat), 322-376 (actions left, the free Move, Hope held), 383-413 (projects as seen)
findings.what_happens: Each explainer is a one-shot drpgWindow built from a read at open; explain.mjs imports nothing from live.mjs and registers no hook that rebuilds an open explainer. The windows print live facts - 'You have 2 of 2 actions left', 'You hold 3 of 6 Hope', each pool's 'held / max', 'Search Tokens here: 2 of 3', the room - and these go stale the moment the clock, a pool or a sheet changes, until the window is closed and opened again. The owner's standing rule of 20.11.2026 (BRIEF.md) is that windows redraw at once when what they show changes.
findings.failure_scenario: A new player clicks the action strip to read what it means, leaves the window open, Searches the room, and the window beside the strip still says 'You have 2 of 2 actions left' while the strip says 1.
findings.expected: An explainer that shows a number either redraws when that number changes (keepLive over the clock, the pools, the actor and the room), or carries no number and points at the widget that does.
findings.refutation_tried: Looked for keepLive, alreadyOpen or a Hooks.on in explain.mjs (none; its imports at 26-37 hold none of live.mjs), and for a caller that rebuilds an open explainer (explainOnce 476-482 only closes the old before opening a new one on the next click). Whether the owner counts a help window under the rule is the owner's; the window does print live values, so it is written here. Probe 43 was not read (no probe-43.json).

findings.title: With only an Assistant GM connected, the primary-GM hold of core.permissions is tried and, by the module's own reading of Foundry, refused - logged, told to nobody
findings.where: scripts/enforced.mjs:557-577 (holdPermissions: isPrimaryGm and the switch, no role test), 579-584 (again on every core.permissions update), 1021-1026 (at ready); scripts/utils.mjs:485-496 (an Assistant GM is primary with no full Gamemaster connected); scripts/enforced.mjs:813-820 (canGiveBack: 'Foundry lets only a full Gamemaster write core.permissions')
findings.what_happens: holdPermissions writes `core.permissions` from whichever GM is primary. primaryGmId picks an Assistant GM when no full Gamemaster is connected. The same file says, for Give back, that Foundry lets only a full Gamemaster write that setting and that an Assistant GM's write threw. So on a session where an Assistant GM is primary and the stored permissions are not as held (the switch turned on, or the hold never run by a full GM), keepOriginal writes the module's record, the `game.settings.set("core", "permissions")` throws, and the error goes to the console and the Debug log at every ready and every permissions update. Nobody gets a notice, and the players keep browsing and uploading files for that session.
findings.failure_scenario: An Assistant GM runs a session while the owner is away, on a world where the file-permission switch was turned on since the owner last loaded it: the players can still open a file browser, and the Assistant GM's Debug log holds a red 'Could not hold the file permissions' line each load with no word on screen.
findings.expected: The hold asks the same role canGiveBack asks, and an Assistant-GM primary either leaves the row for a full Gamemaster and says so, or is told why the files are not held.
findings.refutation_tried: Looked for a role test on the road (holdPermissions, onWorldSettingUpdated, applyEnforced): none. The Foundry rule is the module's own reading at enforced.mjs:814-816, not read on v14 here, so this stays suspected; LIVE-E79-11 is the nearest live item (which roads v14 opens for a player) and does not ask it. With a full Gamemaster ever primary the stored value is already held and nothing is written, so the road needs the situation above.

findings.title: game.drpg.manageItems("name or id") is not normalised: the one API function whose actor parameter has a default beside an options bag
findings.where: scripts/api.mjs:1668-1685 (actorPosition), 564 (manageItems: openItemManager); scripts/gm-items.mjs:331 (`openItemManager(actor = null, { give = null } = {})`), 361-400 (the target used as an actor)
findings.what_happens: actorPosition reads a function's parameter text. When it holds a `{`, it answers 0 only when the first parameter is literally `actor`, so `actor = null, { give = null } = {}` answers -1 and the function is handed on unwrapped. api.mjs's note promises that every API function taking an actor positionally accepts an actor, an id or a name; for manageItems a string reaches openItemManager as `target`, and the window is built around it (`recipientOptions(students, target.id)` with an undefined id, `holdingsHtml(target)`, `keyChoices(target, ...)`). A static pass over the 418 names on game.drpg finds this the only one so affected.
findings.failure_scenario: A GM's macro `game.drpg.manageItems("Aoi")` opens the item window with no student picked or throws inside it, where `game.drpg.killCharacter("Aoi")` works.
findings.expected: The same coercion as every other actor-taking entry (the parameter named `actor`, with or without a default).
findings.refutation_tried: Read openItemManager for its own coercion (none: `actor ?? students[0]`). Ran actorPosition's rule in Python over the definitions of the names api.mjs hands on: openItemManager is the only one with `actor` among its parameters and -1 as the answer. The exact symptom (a throw or a blank recipient) was not run.

l1.what: Whether an Assistant GM can write core.permissions on Foundry 14.370, and what the hold does when an Assistant GM is the primary
recipe: Log in as an Assistant GM alone (no full Gamemaster connected) on a world with the file-permission switch on
Before that, as the full Gamemaster, give FILES_BROWSE back to the Player role in Foundry's permission window, then log out
As the Assistant GM, reload and read the console and game.drpg Debug log for 'Could not hold the file permissions'
As a player, try to open a file browser (a journal image)

l1.settles_if: A refused write and a working file browser for the player confirm finding 4; a written value and a closed browser refute it
